title: Tech Note: Identifying an XML Document's Type
author: David Adams
featured_technology: DOM Get XML information (PUBLIC ID / SYSTEM ID)

historical_commentary.text: This note shows how to distinguish XML document types (using XHTML's four DTD variants as a worked example) by inspecting the root element name, namespace attribute, and DOCTYPE public/system IDs via 4D's DOM commands. It is a period piece both technically (4D's classic DOM XML API) and topically (XHTML 1.0/1.1 DTD-based versioning was largely abandoned industry-wide in favor of HTML5's much simpler doctype), but the general strategy of layered document-type sniffing via root element, namespace, and DTD identifiers remains a conceptually valid technique for XML-based format detection.
related_updates: XHTML 1.0/1.1 and DTD-based document typing have been superseded industry-wide by HTML5, which does not use this DOCTYPE/public-ID scheme
4D's classic DOM XML commands remain available for backward compatibility but are less central to modern 4D development, which includes native JSON support
